title: Kestrel Dispensing Standard: Short-Fill Allowance on Prescriptions Strength-Error Remakes
content:
Where the wrong-strength fill of a Kestrel Prescriptions record was itself dispensed short, the strength-error short-fill allowance gives the patient extra days on the remake.

## Clause

The strength-error short-fill allowance looks at the owed-balance entry booked for the wrong-strength fill on the fill ledger:

1. owed units booked **at least equal to** the units dispensed on that fill give **3 days**;
2. **fewer** owed units booked **but more than zero** give **1 day**;
3. a wrong-strength fill dispensed complete, with no owed units booked for it, gives no days.

Each allowance day adds the prescribed daily units — the prescription's written quantity divided by its written days supply — to the strength-error remake quantity.

## Cases (hypothetical wrong-strength fill of 30 units dispensed, 2 prescribed daily units)

| Owed units booked for the wrong-strength fill | Comparison with 30 | Allowance days | Units added |
|---|---|---|---|
| 30 | equal | 3 | 6 |
| 45 | more | 3 | 6 |
| 29 | fewer, above zero | 1 | 2 |
| none (dispensed complete) | — | 0 | 0 |

## Note on the owed-balance entry

The entry that counts is the owed-balance entry booked for the wrong-strength fill itself; its owed units as booked are compared, whether or not the balance has since been completed or cancelled.
